name: Simple Fatoora
author: Future Base

sections.description:
Simple Fatoora connects your WooCommerce store to the Simple Fatoora e‑invoicing platform and automatically creates compliant e‑invoices for your orders.

The plugin is designed for stores that must comply with ZATCA Phase 2 (Saudi Arabia) and similar VAT regulations. It can generate both simplified invoices and VAT invoices, attach invoice details to customer emails, and keep your WooCommerce orders in sync with Simple Fatoora.

Key features

  • Automatic invoice creation when an order reaches a chosen status (for example, Processing or Completed).
  • Support for both simplified invoices and VAT invoices.
  • ZATCA Phase 2–ready QR codes (generated by the Simple Fatoora service).
  • Company / VAT checkout option:
    • Customers can mark that the order is for a company.
    • Additional company name and VAT number fields are collected.
    • These values are sent to Simple Fatoora as client_name and client_vat_number for VAT invoices.
  • Order‑level sync status and invoice details accessible from the WooCommerce order screen.
  • Optional invoice information block added to relevant customer emails.
  • Simple configuration screen inside WooCommerce → Settings → Simple Fatoora.

You need an active Simple Fatoora account and API key to use this plugin.
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin:
    • Upload the ZIP file via Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin, or
    • Copy the simple-fatoora folder into /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate Simple Fatoora through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to WooCommerce → Settings → Simple Fatoora.
  4. Enter your Simple Fatoora API key and connect.
  5. In the Invoice Settings tab:
    • Choose the WooCommerce order status where invoices should be created automatically.
    • Optionally set Terms and Conditions and Custom Notes to appear on your invoices.
  6. Place a test order to confirm that an invoice is created in Simple Fatoora.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Simple Fatoora account?

Yes. This plugin is a connector between WooCommerce and the Simple Fatoora e‑invoicing service. You must have a valid Simple Fatoora account and API key.

Does this plugin generate QR codes by itself?

No. The QR code and ZATCA Phase 2 compliance are handled by the Simple Fatoora backend. The plugin sends the order data to Simple Fatoora, and the service returns the compliant invoice and QR code.

How are invoices created automatically?

In the Invoice Settings tab you can choose one WooCommerce order status (for example, Processing). When an order reaches that status, the plugin sends it to Simple Fatoora and creates an invoice automatically. The plugin also watches for Completed orders as a fallback.

How does the company / VAT option work on checkout?

On the checkout page, customers see a checkbox such as:

  • “This order is for a company – VAT invoice” (English), or
  • “هذا الطلب لشركة – فاتورة ضريبية” (Arabic).

If they tick the box, two extra fields appear:

  • Company name
  • Company VAT number

These fields are required when the box is checked. The values are sent to Simple Fatoora as the client name and VAT number for VAT invoices, and the invoice is marked with client_type = 1 and invoice_type = 1.

If the box is not checked, the plugin sends a simplified invoice (client_type = 2, invoice_type = 0) based on the billing name.

Can I disable automatic invoice generation or email invoice details?

In the current version, automatic invoice generation is always enabled once the API key is connected. You can still control when the invoice is created by choosing the order status in the Invoice Settings tab.

Invoice information is added to relevant customer emails (for the chosen status and Completed) whenever an invoice exists for that order.

Does this plugin store invoices in WordPress?

No. Invoices, QR codes, and related compliance data are stored on the Simple Fatoora platform. The plugin stores only minimal tracking information on WooCommerce orders (such as invoice number and sync status).
sections.changelog:
1.4.4

  • Added company / VAT invoice option on checkout.
  • Added order meta mapping to send client_type, invoice_type, client_name, and client_vat_number based on customer choice.
  • Improved settings handling for automatic invoice status and disconnect behavior.
  • Updated styles for the settings screen to better match Simple Fatoora branding.

1.4.3

  • Improved styling for the settings page.
  • Added configurable “auto‑generate invoice” status.
  • Added option to include invoice information in customer emails.

1.4.2

  • Internal improvements to settings layout and error handling.

1.4.1

  • Initial integration of the new Simple Fatoora settings tab UI.
  • Compatibility updates for WooCommerce and WordPress 6.8.
